newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian shares pick up, further gains seen.
newsitem.headline: Estonian shares pick up, further gains seen.

text.p: Estonian shares picked up on Friday and dealers said small gains were expected on Monday.
The Talse picked up 0.27 percent to close at 256.69 with 34 million kroons of shares traded on the main list.
"It was an average Friday trade with lower volumes, but the market has bottomed out and some larger investors are starting to get back in," one trader said.
"The mood on the market seems to be changing a little," another dealer said.
Hansapank turned over 13.3 million kroons and gained 2.00 kroons to close at 133.00 kroons.
Forekspank turned over 7.4 million kroons to be 0.90 kroons higher at 182.50 kroons.
"Prices should be stable to higher on Monday, but there are some sellers in individual stocks which may hold them down," he added.
The over-the-counter market saw five million kroons of shares change hands with industralist Norma the most most active stock.
Norma saw 2.4 million kroons of shares change hands to be 0.05 kroons higher for a close at 73.70 kroons.
After the market closed Norma released its April results which showed a net profit of 9.6 million kroons on turnover of 42.3 million kroons. Its net profit in March was 9.4 million kroons.
"We should see more action on this stock on Monday, as the numbers are good," a free market trader said. -- David Mardiste, Tallinn newsroom +372 630 8400 reuters@reuters.ee
